# PREFACE

Traditionally, refractories are considered a unique industrial product used primarily in basic industries such as iron, steel, glass, cement and pottery. Being complex multi-component systems in most cases, they are difficult to predict than other materials using simple scientific methods and principles. It is quite an unknown material to the general public and also to other industries.

During the last two decades, a significant amount of attention has been paid to refractory ceramics as results could be predicted fairly accurately depending on the product and application. Although not much progress has been made in brick making, except in MgO–C bricks, significant progress has been made in monolithic refractories in materials, products and applications in the last two decades. The unique advantage of monolithic refractories is its continuous body. Without any joints, it provides better structural integrity and can be installed with relative ease requiring labors in less numbers and skill.

At present, there is a dearth of literature on monolithic refractories, except for a few company-sponsored books which are biased towards their own products. Thus, this book provides a basic understanding of the principles of monolithic refractory formulation, manufacture and application. The topics covered include the selection

of raw materials, product formulation for specific applications, and the principles behind the effective use of the products during application.

The book is arranged in chronological order, beginning with raw materials and proceeding to the relative order of use. The book is organized according to the methods of application of refractories, namely, castables, pumpables, plastics, ramming mixes, gunning mixes, mortars, coatings and dry vibratables. The chapter on castables deals with binders used in recent years for castable formulations which include calcium aluminate cements, hydrated alumina, and colloids, with their specific characteristics. The advantages and disadvantages of the different binders and their methods of application are also discussed in detail. The sections on ramming and gunning mixes deal with both conventional and the recently developed binder systems and their special behavior. Mortars, coatings and dry vibratables are dealt with using specific applications. Their advantages and the appropriate selection of the particular products are examined. Apart from the product area, the book also deals with the manufacture of monolithic mixes and pre-cast shapes, the evaluation and testing of refractory properties, system design, and application since the performance of monolithic refractories depends vastly on the proper installation and heating procedure before use. All these considerations are dealt with in this book to ensure that the refractory performs as desired.

Since refractories come into contact with different types of slag, a chapter is devoted to the discussion of slag reactions, especially those monolithic refractories in the blast furnace cast-house troughs, steel ladles and tundishes that come into contact with slags. The book was compiled using various sources, such as, books, periodicals, personnel communications and most recently, applied work in the field.

It is impossible to thank every individual who helped in the writing of this book. Nevertheless, some of them deserved special mention for their invaluable help rendered in its preparation. Dr.
